key_insight: You can extract reliable Q-value estimates from a behavior-cloned policy and use those estimates to gate online reinforcement learning, enabling safe, targeted improvement on robot hardware without overwriting good demonstrated behaviors.
problem_solved: Behavior Cloning (BC) lacks a self-guided mechanism for safe online improvement: naive offline-to-online updates can overwrite good demonstrated actions due to distribution mismatch, causing regressions when deployed on robots.
method: Q-estimation from BC: derive Q-value estimates from the pretrained behavior-cloned policy and offline data to quantify action quality.
Q-gating during online RL: allow policy updates only when candidate actions have higher estimated Q-values than the preserved BC actions, preventing replacement of good demonstrated behavior.
Conservative, efficient offline-to-online workflow: combine extracted Q-values with online exploration to focusedly improve performance on-robot while maintaining safety and sample efficiency.
impact: Q2RL enables safe, sample-efficient on-robot reinforcement learning by preserving proven offline behaviors and only applying online updates that are estimated to improve returns — reducing regressions and speeding real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: BC model -> Q extraction -> Q-gating module -> online RL on robot
Before/after performance plot: policy reward over online iterations comparing standard offline-to-online vs Q2RL (shows no regressions and faster gains)
Action-gating schematic: example state with BC action highlighted and candidate action allowed/blocked based on estimated Q-value
Robot-in-loop photo/icon with callouts for safety, sample efficiency, and preserved demonstrated behaviors
paper_title: When Life Gives You BC, Make Q-functions: Extracting Q-values from Behavior Cloning for On-Robot Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Lakshita Dodeja, Ondrej Biza, Shivam Vats, Stephen Hart, Stefanie Tellex
